text: asked QC5-001: J's ruling 4 (15 October) asks that the C5b packets carry the rule and the amended declarations with their members' quotes. Each packet must also hold account.md, figure-C5.md and propositions.jsonl (35,073 bytes), the instruction and three rooms under the 51,200-byte ceiling. The 36 amended declarations, whole, come to about 40 KB before their quotes, so they do not fit even split across the three readers. I served instead: the rule (its reading parts and the C5a-02 scope paragraph); the 40 sentences of all 36 declarations that hold a word from the rule's lists, which are the sentences the rule puts in question, split by declaration across the readers, each reader saying whether each sentence stands; and the 72 Stigmergy records drawn at C5a-01, 24 per reader, to code blind. Ten declarations have no sentence in question and are not served (Keying, Sensemaking, Collective efficacy, Reciprocity, Neo-tribes, Completion ritual, Collective memory, Transition, Critical mass, Contention). Not served: the whole declarations, their other sentences and the quotes those carry. To fit, the three rooms are served as their facts and 7 passages each by cite.py's seeded draw, without their forests. Is this an acceptable second reading for J's ruling 4? If not, which should give way: the rooms' passages, or a further reader for the whole declarations after the dispatch? | meanwhile: The packets go out as built, and the dispatch can run on them. The check leg scores the readers' sentence verdicts and codes against mine. If you rule otherwise, the packets are rebuilt before the dispatch, or the remaining declarations go to the reader you name.

The three packets built (packets.py files --stage C5): C5-reader-1 50,993 bytes, C5-reader-2 51,018, C5-reader-3 51,035, under the 51,200 ceiling. Each holds 0-read-me-first.md (served sha256 of account.md 77b5e35d..., the instruction verbatim, the second reading), account.md, figure-C5.md, propositions.jsonl, rooms.md (cardinals, luciomains, mysterydungeon: facts and 7 seeded passages each) and second-reading.md (the rule; that reader's share of the 40 sentences in question; the Stigmergy code definitions and the 24 records of one member theme, blind). Each carries the end line; none names my notes. run_manifest.json's C5 entry pins the packets' sha256. QC5-001 asks the handler whether the sentences in question are an acceptable second reading of the declarations for J's ruling 4; meanwhile the packets go out as built.

figure-C5.md: the paragraph on what it leaves out named the tentative arrow A21 by id, and the check reads every arrow id in the figure as drawn (two errors: no instance, not in the model). It now names the arrow by its ends (P08 to P21). The figure was written again, the three packets rebuilt (50,998, 51,023 and 51,040 bytes), and the C5 manifest entry's digests read again (c5b_manifest_entry.py --packets). validate.py C5: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Close of C5b, the readers' build. run_manifest.json C5 entry (readers claude-opus-5-5, one per packet, via the CLI; three; seed 20261015; account.md sha256 77b5e35d..., figure, propositions, claims, return spec and the three packets pinned). author_claims.jsonl: nine claims. Rooms by rule (logged before the draw, revised twice for the 50 KB ceiling before any page was read for content): cardinals (told), luciomains (told with a residue), mysterydungeon (late side, which the account visits least: 2 rooms against 7); each served as its facts and 7 passages by cite.py's seeded draw, no forest. RETURN-C5.md: the stage's return line plus declarations and codes for J's ruling 4. The second reading: the rule, the 40 sentences of the 36 amended declarations that the rule's word lists put in question (from the ledger, split by declaration across readers), and the 72 Stigmergy records, 24 per reader, to code blind. Not served: the whole declarations and their other sentences and quotes; QC5-001 asks the handler whether this suffices, and the packets go out meanwhile. Packets 50,998, 51,023 and 51,040 bytes. Slips: order (rooms and RETURN before the manifest entry and claims), a no-op heredoc command, two parallel Edits to one script, the figure naming A21 (fixed, packets rebuilt). validate.py C5: 0 errors, 0 warnings; head 2,994 words, links resolve. Next: done.sh C5 --cut packets-out.
